newsitem.title: UK: Conoco's UK N.Sea Boulton gas field gets go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Conoco's UK N.Sea Boulton gas field gets go-ahead.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) on Tuesday gave approval for the development of the Boulton gas field in the North Sea's southern basin.
Boulton, located in block 44/21a, 170 km north east of the terminal of Theddlethorpe in Lincolnshire, will start production in the second quarter of 1998.
The field operator will be Conoco (UK) Ltd, which holds 46 percent of the equity. The other participants are LASMO North Sea Plc (44.5 percent) and British Borneo Oil and Gas Limited (9.5 percent).
Recoverable reserves are put at 165 billion cubic feet of wet gas, and production is expected to peak at 90 million cubic feet a day.
The field will be be developed by one platform, which will not normally be manned, serving two production wells.

Gas from Boulton will flow to the nearby Murdoch platform. There it will be compressed for onward transmission through the existing Caister Murdoch System (CMS) pipeline to the Conoco terminal at Theddlethorpe.

British Borneo and LASMO sold their share of Boulton gas to Eastern Natural Gas (Trading) Limited, part of Hanson plc, in August. Conoco is keeping its share for current and future customer requirements.
